intro: Google Docs on a Mac runs in your browser, not in a separate Mac app. Chrome or Edge gives you offline editing, and Safari does not. This guide covers setup, templates, shortcuts, reviews and Gemini access, plus where Lazur helps while you draft grant letters and reports.

Use ⌘/ for the shortcut list, and Suggesting mode when you want reviewers to propose changes.

blocks.text: Is there a Google Docs app for Mac?

No, not a native one that I could find. Google Docs runs in a browser tab on your Mac. You open docs.google.com, sign in with your Google account, and work there. I found no native Mac Docs app in the Google pages I checked.

Drive for desktop is the one Mac install that matters here. It puts your Drive files in Finder, so your grant folders sit next to your other Mac files. It needs macOS Ventura 13.0 or higher. To check your version, open the Apple menu > About This Mac.
Drive for desktop only syncs files. Editing still happens in the browser tab, so keep Docs open while you draft.
Which browser works best for Google Docs on Mac?

Google's system requirements page says to use one of the two most recent versions of your browser. Cookies and JavaScript must be on. Other browsers may work, but some features can be missing. The page does not name Mac browsers, so that rule is the one to follow.

For offline work, pick Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. Offline editing needs one of those two. If you use Safari only, you can still edit Docs online, but you lose offline editing. That matters on a train, in a community hall with weak Wi-Fi, or during a donor event where the connection drops.

blocks.title: Offline needs Chrome or Edge
blocks.text: Safari-only Mac users cannot use offline editing in Google Docs. Install Chrome or Edge before you need it, not during deadline week.
How to set up offline Google Docs in Chrome or Edge

items: Install Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge if you do not have it yet.
Open a normal window. Private browsing does not work for offline setup.
Sign in with the Google account you use for nonprofit work.
Turn on offline access. Our [offline mode guide](/how-to/turn-on-offline-mode-in-google-docs) walks through the steps.
Open the files you need while you are online, so they are ready later.

blocks.text: Two limits catch people out. Only one account per browser profile can have offline enabled. If you run a personal Google account and a nonprofit account on one Mac, make a separate Chrome profile for each. Very large files may also fail to sync. Google suggests splitting them into smaller documents.
Your Workspace administrator can turn off offline access for some accounts. If the option is missing, ask your admin before you spend an hour on troubleshooting.
How to start a grant proposal from a Google Docs template

Templates save the most time on repeat work. Most fundraisers rewrite the same organization history, board list and budget narrative for each funder. A template holds the structure, so you only change the parts that differ.

There are two ways to open one. Open Template Gallery from the top right of the Docs home screen, pick a template, and a copy opens. Or, inside an open document, go to File > New > From a template, scroll, choose one, and click Insert.
Watch for one catch. If the document already has content, the template opens in new document tabs. It does not replace your text. Some template features only work with work or school accounts.

Build your own template once a proposal works. Then make a copy for each new funder. Read [how to create a template in Google Docs](/how-to/create-a-template-in-google-docs) and [how to make a copy of a document in Google Docs](/how-to/make-a-copy-of-a-document-in-google-docs).
Worked example: three funder letters from one master file

Say you send letters of inquiry to three foundations this month. Keep one master template with the organization history, board list and standard closing. Make a copy for each funder, and name it with the funder and the date. Change only the program details and the ask in each copy.

Before each copy goes out, check the funder's word limit. Use the [word count guide](/how-to/see-word-count-in-google-docs) to see the count while you edit. Then read the copy once out loud. Mistakes show up faster that way.
Keyboard shortcuts for Google Docs on Mac
Google's shortcut list is long. You do not need all of it. These are the ones that save the most time on grant drafts.

items: ⌘/ opens the full shortcut list. Check it first when you forget a key.
⌘K inserts a link, or edits the link under your cursor. Use it for your donation page and impact report.
⌘⇧H opens find and replace. Swap an old program name for a new one across the whole draft.
⌘⌥M adds a comment to the selected text. Ask a colleague about a budget line without changing it.
⌘⌥⇧H opens revision history. Use it when someone deletes a paragraph you need back.
⌥ Return opens the link where your cursor sits.

blocks.text: Mac shortcuts can clash with other apps or with your keyboard settings. If a shortcut does nothing, open the list with ⌘/ and check the exact keys.
How to review edits from a board member or grant officer
Reviews go wrong when two people edit the same paragraph. One change overwrites another, and nobody knows which version is right. Set the rules before you share the file.

Ask reviewers to use Suggesting mode. Open the mode menu at the top right of the toolbar and choose Suggesting. Each change then appears as a suggestion that you accept or reject. Read [how to suggest edits in Google Docs](/how-to/suggest-edits-in-google-docs) and [how to accept or reject suggestions in Google Docs](/how-to/accept-or-reject-suggestions-in-google-docs).
Use comments for questions. A comment does not touch the text. Select the words and press ⌘⌥M, then type the question. The [comment guide](/how-to/add-a-comment-in-google-docs) shows the full steps.
Mistake to avoid: giving a funder's reviewer edit access. Give them comment access, or send a PDF once the draft is final.
What Gemini in Google Docs needs in 2026

Google's April 22, 2026 update added Gemini tools to Docs. The set includes Help me create, Help me write, Match writing style and Match document format. Suggested edits from Help me write stay visible only to the editor until someone approves them.

Not every account gets them. Google lists Business Standard and Plus, Enterprise Standard and Plus, Education Plus, Google AI Pro and Ultra, and some add-on plans. Your Workspace admin must turn on Gemini for Workspace in Drive.

Rollout began April 22, 2026 for Rapid Release domains and May 6, 2026 for Scheduled Release domains. Promotional access to higher Match limits ran through July 15, 2026. Per-user limits apply after that date.
If your account is not on that list, Gemini will not show up in Docs. Lazur is a separate Mac app. It does not add or replace Gemini in Google Docs.
How long grant writing takes, and what the surveys say

Grant writing time varies, and the surveys disagree. In GrantStation's 2023 survey of 2,463 respondents, 70% said writing the largest grant took two days to two weeks. The same report's time section says 54% spent more than three days writing. Both figures come from one report, and the gap is not explained.

Instrumentl, a grant software vendor, surveyed more than 300 grant professionals. It reports an average of two weeks to write and submit a proposal. The same survey says 46% of respondents use AI to draft proposals, the most common AI task. Treat it as a vendor survey, not a neutral benchmark.
A 2015 PLOS ONE study estimated 116 hours of principal investigator effort per proposal. It surveyed 113 astronomers and 82 psychologists, not nonprofit fundraisers. Use it as a rough proxy only.
For your own planning, track one proposal from first draft to submission. Log the hours, the people and the days. Your own log will beat any survey for your team's next deadline.
Where Lazur fits while you work in Google Docs
Lazur lives in the notch on your Mac. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud.
Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before the next step.
That split matters in a grant draft. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. You keep control of the text and the settings, and Lazur helps you find the next step.

Dictation is the other half. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app, including Google Docs in your browser. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots help with repeat phrases, such as your mission line and program names.
How to ask Lazur about your draft
Lazur sees the page, so ask about what is in front of you. Try asking what a paragraph says about the budget. Lazur answers out loud, and your eyes stay on the draft.
Be specific. Asking where the mode menu is gets a useful pointer. Asking Lazur to fix the whole proposal is too wide. Ask about one section at a time, then check each change yourself.

Lazur drafts and types text too. Ask for a first pass at a thank-you note, and Lazur types it at your cursor. Read the donor's name, the gift amount and the date before you send anything. Drafts can get those details wrong.
Privacy and donor data on screen
Donor records are sensitive. Before you ask Lazur about a document with donor names or gift amounts, check your organization's data rules. Lazur only listens and looks while you hold the shortcut.

Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, and that memory stays on your Mac.
Common mistakes in Google Docs grant drafts
Most of these mistakes cost time on the day before a deadline. Fixing them in advance is cheap.

items: Working in Safari only, then expecting offline editing to work.
Using a private window for offline setup.
Keeping several copies of one proposal in Drive with names like final v2. Keep one master and copy it for each funder.
Letting two people edit the same paragraph in Editing mode at once.
Giving a funder's reviewer edit access when comment access would do.
Forgetting that a template opens in a new tab when the document already has content.
Trusting an AI draft without checking figures, names and dates.

blocks.text: Fluent AI text can hide a wrong number or a misspelled funder name. Check every figure against your source file before it goes out.
How to name and store grant files in Drive

Name files for the funder, the document type and the date, such as funder name, letter of inquiry and the month. A name like final FINAL v3 wastes time later. Keep one folder for each active funder. Store the master template in its own folder.
If you use Drive for desktop, the same folders appear in Finder. Use Finder search with the funder's name when you need one file quickly.
What to do next

items: Check your browser. Use Chrome or Edge if you need offline editing.
Turn on offline access and test it with one document before a deadline.
Build one master template, then make a copy for each funder.
Read the shortcut list with ⌘/ and learn the handful you use most.
Try Lazur on one real task, such as a thank-you note or a word count check.

faq.question: Is there a Google Docs app for Mac?
faq.answer: Not a native one that I could find. Google Docs runs in a browser tab. Drive for desktop syncs your Drive files to Finder and needs macOS Ventura 13.0 or higher. Editing still happens in the browser.

faq.question: Does Google Docs work offline on a Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, in Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge with the Google Docs Offline extension. Use a normal window, not private browsing. Only one account per browser profile can have offline enabled, and an administrator can turn it off for some accounts.

faq.question: Can I edit Google Docs offline in Safari?
faq.answer: Not offline. Offline editing requires Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. Safari users can still open and edit Docs online when they have a connection.

faq.question: Can I use my own template in Google Docs?
faq.answer: Yes. Build a master document, then make a copy for each funder. Some template features only work with work or school accounts, so check your account type first.

faq.question: Do I need a paid plan to use Gemini in Google Docs?
faq.answer: Yes. Google lists only paid plans for these features: Business Standard and Plus, Enterprise Standard and Plus, Education Plus, Google AI Pro and Ultra, and some add-on plans. Your admin must also turn on Gemini for Workspace in Drive.

faq.question: Is Lazur an add-on or plugin for Google Docs?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnerships with any app maker.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons or edit my grant draft?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides you one click at a time and waits for each click. It can point at things, answer questions out loud, and draft or type text. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur send my donor data to AI providers?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so it can answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Check your organization's data rules before you share donor records.

faq.question: Why do grant writing time estimates disagree?
faq.answer: Surveys define the task and the sample differently. GrantStation's 2023 report gives 70% for two days to two weeks, but its time section gives 54% for more than three days. The Instrumentl two-week average comes from a vendor survey. The PLOS ONE figure covers academics, not fundraisers.
